title: Delegated IAM Patterns by Environment — Privilege Separation & Evidence Flow
body:
Overview:
This working doc defines a set of delegated IAM patterns that we recommend for each deployment environment (hosted, dedicated, private) with a focus on privilege separation, just-in-time elevation, and reliable evidence collection for audits and SIEM ingestion. The goal is to reduce blast radius of admin capabilities while making it straightforward to produce verifiable audit bundles for compliance reviews.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to control-plane and runtime management operations (create/modify/delete models, network changes, capacity operations, key operations).
- Assumes RBAC v2 baseline is in place (role objects, permission sets, resource scoping).
- We aim for automated evidence capture and SIEM-friendly exports (JSON schema_v3).
- This doc contains pragmatic patterns, recommended responsibilities, plus example policy snippets for reference.

Summary of environment-specific guidance:
1) Hosted (multi-tenant Redwood API):
  - Principle: Minimally-privileged central ops, customer separation by tenant scoping.
  - Roles: Hosted-OrgAdmin (rare), Hosted-SRE (operational runbooks), Hosted-Audit (read-only logs), Support-Scoped (customer-level ticket ops).
  - Delegation pattern: Use tenant-scoped service accounts for support tasks, with short-lived delegation tokens (max 1h). No direct long-lived keys for humans.
  - Evidence flow: All delegated actions must produce an evidence bundle (action_id, initiator, token_id, before/after resource snapshot). Bundle stored in internal evidence-store S3 with KMS encryption and immutability flag.

2) Dedicated (reserved capacity for single customer):
  - Principle: Customer isolation, but Redwood operators need constrained maintenance access.
  - Roles: Dedicated-CustAdmin (customer-managed), Dedicated-Operator (Redwood limited maintenance), Dedicated-Audit.
  - Delegation pattern: Dedicated-Operator requests JIT access from Dedicated-CustAdmin via approval workflow (Slack + ticketing). Approvals create ephemeral RBAC bindings (ttl 15m–2h) issued by the control plane.
  - Evidence flow: Same evidence bundle requirement as hosted but with customer visibility toggle: customer-specified evidence retention policy may be applied.

3) Private (VPC / on-prem):
  - Principle: Customer-managed control plane; Redwood provides optionally-managed support with strict scope.
  - Roles: Private-LocalAdmin (customer), Private-Redwood-Limited (Redwood support), Private-Audit.
  - Delegation pattern: Support actions require customer out-of-band authorization (signed incident ticket). Delegation tokens are bound to a remote ephemeral certificate (mTLS client cert) and are logged with certificate fingerprint.
  - Evidence flow: Evidence bundles must be exportable to customer SIEM; metadata fields must align to schema_v3 mapping.

Privilege separation and delegation building blocks:
- Role composition: Build small permission primitives (e.g., model:list, model:modify-config, infra:reboot-node) and compose roles by granting sets. Avoid role proliferation by using attribute-based scoping (resource.owner, resource.env).
- Ephemeral delegation tokens: Tokens are minted by the control plane after an approval step. Tokens include policy pointer and audit_id. TTLs default to 1h, configurable per role.
- Just-in-time (JIT) elevation: Integrate with ticketing (Jira) and chat ops (Slack) for human approvals; automated JIT for scheduled maintenance windows.
- Privilege escalation guardrails: Every elevation must create a signed authorization record stored in evidence-store. Tamper-evidence via HMAC over the record and recorded KMS key id.

Evidence bundle contents (required fields):
- evidence_id: opaque UUID
- audit_id: correlates to control-plane audit log event
- initiator: user/service principal canonical id
- role_snapshot: list of RBAC roles active at time of action (stringified)
- token_id / cert_fingerprint: identifier for delegation credential used
- env: hosted | dedicated | private
- target_resource: resource canonical path (e.g., projects/123/models/mymy)
- action: canonical action name (model:update-config)
- timestamp_utc: ISO8601
- before_snapshot: base64 gzipped JSON (optional)
- after_snapshot: base64 gzipped JSON (optional)
- signature: HMAC-SHA256(KMS-key-id, bundle_contents)

Audit log schema_v3 (recommended SIEM mapping):
- event_id (string)
- event_time (ISO8601)
- actor_id (string)
- actor_type (human | service)
- action (string)
- action_category (control_plane | runtime | data_access)
- resource_type (model | node | network | secret)
- resource_id (string)
- resource_owner (tenant id)
- env (hosted|dedicated|private)
- correlation_id (audits can tie multiple events)
- evidence_ref (s3://... or evidence-store://...)
- result (success | failure)
- metadata (free-form map as JSON string)

Notes on SIEM export mechanics:
- Export format: newline-delimited JSON, one event per line, compressed with gzip for transfer.
- Delivery: push to customer SIEM via syslog over TLS or pull from our secure S3 with signed URLs.
- Field normalization: All timestamps normalized to UTC and RFC3339. Actor and resource canonical IDs should be stable (UUIDs).

Evidence automation playbook (high-level steps):
1) Action occurs (API call, operator CLI) -> control plane creates audit event and assigns audit_id.
2) Delegation metadata appended if action was via delegated token (token_id, requester_ticket).
3) Snapshot hook invoked for supported resources; snapshot saved as gzipped JSON to evidence-store with evidence_id.
4) Signature/HMAC calculated using evidence-kms key; attached to bundle.
5) Index record added to audit-index (searchable), with pointer to evidence-store and SIEM-ready event emitted.
6) Retention and deletion policies: evidence default retention 2 years (hosted), customizable for dedicated/private per contract.

Example RBAC primitive list (non-exhaustive):
- model:list
- model:view-config
- model:update-config
- model:rollback
- infra:node-reboot
- infra:drain-node
- network:update-firewall
- secret:read (restricted via KMS policy)

Policy template (example: minimal Dedicated-Operator role in pseudo-JSON):
{
  "role_name": "Dedicated-Operator",
  "description": "Temporary maintenance role for Redwood operators on dedicated customers",
  "permissions": ["model:list", "infra:node-reboot", "infra:drain-node"],
  "resource_scope": "projects/{{customer_id}}/*",
  "ttl": "2h"
}

Operational considerations and open questions:
- How do we handle evidence for non-snapshotable resources (e.g., live TCP connections)? Recommendation: capture control-plane metadata and post-incident traces.
- Who rotates evidence-kms keys and how often? Propose quarterly rotation with key-usage logs.
- Retention differences driven by customer contract: make retention configurable and surfaced in the Dedicated onboarding checklist.

Next steps (action items):
- Security: finalize schema_v3 and publish mapping to Splunk/Datadog SIEM teams (owner: Lena Kim) [SEC-5023].
- Infra: implement token minting endpoint with audit_id correlation and TTL enforcement (owner: Miguel Torres) [INF-2348].
- Product: add delegation UI for customer approval flows in Dedicated console (owner: Rajesh Iyer) [PX-1182].

Appendix A — Useful links and references:
- Confluence: IAM reference patterns (link above)
- Jira: SEC-4821, SEC-5023, INF-2348
- GitHub: infra-provisioning PR #912 (example implementation prototype)

This doc is intentionally pragmatic — it is a working source for security, infra, and product to converge on specific enforcement and UI changes. Feedback welcome in the linked Confluence page or directly in the Jira tickets noted above.
